cross_references.label: Consumer Records — Advance Notice Requirement
cross_references.note: §1985.3 requires 10 days advance notice to any consumer whose records are being subpoenaed from a business. Failure to serve required notice renders the SDT unenforceable. Critical for subpoenas to banks, insurers, credit agencies.

cross_references.label: Employee Records — Advance Notice Requirement
cross_references.note: §1985.6 requires 10 days advance notice to any employee whose employment records are subpoenaed. Applies to employment verification records and personnel files held by employers.

cross_references.label: Business Records Deposition Subpoena
cross_references.note: §2020.410 allows non-party records production via custodian declaration without live testimony. The most practical tool for large-scale records collection from hospitals, banks, pension trusts, and government agencies.

cross_references.label: CMIA — Medical Records Disclosure Authorization
cross_references.note: SDTs for medical records must comply with CMIA §56.10's authorized disclosure framework. The SDT falls under §56.10(b)(3) (party to proceeding via subpoena duces tecum) — but consumer notice under §1985.3 is also required.

cross_references.label: Inspection Demands — Party Discovery
cross_references.note: §2031 governs inspection demands directed to parties. The SDT under §1985 is the non-party analog — used when the custodian of relevant records is not a party to the litigation.

cross_references.label: ERISA Civil Enforcement — Federal Discovery for Pension Records
cross_references.note: For pension Trust records in ERISA-governed plans, federal court discovery under ERISA §1132 and FRCP Rules 45/34 may be more appropriate than state SDTs, particularly given potential ERISA preemption of state discovery processes for plan records.

cross_references.label: Motion to Quash or Modify Subpoena
cross_references.note: §1987.1 governs motions by the non-party or the subject of the records to quash or modify an SDT. Grounds: overbreadth, undue burden, privilege, privacy. Knowing this provision is needed to anticipate and overcome challenges to the steward's SDTs.
